And never worship at thy throne,
Watts made this hymn from Psalm 14, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.” They are corrupt; their acts are vile. There is no one who does good. 2The LORD looks down from heaven upon the sons of men to see if any understand, if any seek God. 3All have turned away, they have together become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one. 4Will the workers of iniquity never learn? They devour my people like bread; they refuse to call upon the LORD. … 3 more verses PSALM 14 · ITS FIRST VERSES · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 14
Are sinners now so senseless grown That they thy saints devour? And never worship at thy throne, Nor fear thine awful power? STANZA I
